from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Binomial Distribution", [
            "Binomial distributions count successes in n independent trials.",
            "Remember BINS: Binary, Independent, Number, Success.",
            "The number of trials n is fixed."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        n = 5
        trials = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE) for _ in range(n)])
        for i, trial in enumerate(trials):
            # Using grid positions B1-B5 for 5 trials
            self.place_at_grid(trial, f"B{i+1}", scale_factor=0.8)
            
        success_indices = [1, 3] # Representing 2 successes
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(trials))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        success_group = VGroup(*[trials[i] for i in success_indices])
        self.play(
            success_group.animate.set_color("#32CD32"),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The PMF calculates probability for exactly k successes.",
            "Formula: P(X=k) = C(n, k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k).",
            "Visual histograms show how n and p change shape.",
            "We calculate specific success probabilities.",
            "Parameters define the entire distribution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Probability Mass Function (PMF)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(X=k) = ", "C(n, k)", " \\cdot ", "p^k", " \\cdot ", "(1-p)^{n-k}"
        ).scale(0.9)
        
        # Color specific parts
        formula[3].set_color("#FF6347")
        formula[5].set_color("#4682B4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Introduce PMF, no change to lecture lines
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display the binomial coefficient formula C(n, k).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        c_nk = formula[1].copy()
        self.place_at_grid(c_nk, "B2", 1.5)
        self.play(Write(c_nk))
        self.wait(1)

        # Display the p^k term, coloring p as #FF6347.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        p_k = formula[3].copy()
        self.place_at_grid(p_k, "C2", 1.5)
        self.play(Write(p_k))
        self.wait(1)

        # Display the (1-p)^(n-k) term, coloring (1-p) as #4682B4.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        q_nk = formula[5].copy()
        self.place_at_grid(q_nk, "D2", 1.5)
        self.play(Write(q_nk))
        self.wait(1)

        # Combine all terms into the final PMF formula.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(c_nk), FadeOut(p_k), FadeOut(q_nk))
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "D4", 1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # Flash the complete formula to emphasize the PMF structure.
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Mean equals n times p.",
            "Variance equals n times p times q.",
            "Mean represents the distribution's center.",
            "Variance represents the distribution's spread.",
            "Parameters shift the distribution's mass."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mean and Variance: The Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        mean_formula = MathTex("E[X] = np").scale(1.5)
        var_formula = MathTex("V[X] = np(1-p)").scale(1.5)
        np_part = MathTex("np").set_color("#FFD700")
        q_part = MathTex("(1-p)").set_color("#00BFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(mean_formula))
        self.place_at_grid(mean_formula, 'B2')
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(var_formula))
        self.place_at_grid(var_formula, 'D2')
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=self.grid['B3'], end=self.grid['B2'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow1))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid['D3'], end=self.grid['D2'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow2))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Simple indicator flash
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(mean_formula, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(rect.animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeOut(rect))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Binomial models solve real-world binary problems.", "Quality control uses these models effectively.", "Approximations emerge as n increases."]
        self.setup_layout("Application and Wrap-up", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a real-world example scenario icon (using simple geometric shape instead of unavailable file)
        icon1 = Circle(radius=0.5).set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(icon1, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(icon1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Summarize the binomial application steps
        steps = VGroup(
            Text("1. Define Success", font_size=20),
            Text("2. Check Trials (n)", font_size=20),
            Text("3. Calculate Probability", font_size=20)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(steps, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(steps))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in a 'Conclusion' text to end the section
        conclusion = Text("Conclusion: Binomial -> Normal", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(conclusion))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Define the Bernoulli trial as the foundation: an experiment with exactly two outcomes (Success/Failure) and a constant probability 'p'.
sections.example: Visualizing a coin flip: Heads (Success, p=0.5) vs. Tails (Failure, q=0.5).

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
sections.content: Explain that a Binomial Distribution counts the number of successes in 'n' independent Bernoulli trials. Introduce the mnemonic BINS: Binary, Independent, Number (fixed), Success (constant probability).
sections.example: A robot dog attempting 5 jumps; each jump is either a 'Success' (lands perfectly) or 'Failure' (stumbles).

sections.title: The Probability Mass Function (PMF)
sections.content: Introduce the formula P(X=k) = C(n, k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use a graphical bar chart animation to show how 'n' and 'p' shape the distribution histogram.
sections.example: Calculating the probability of the robot dog landing exactly 3 out of 5 jumps.

sections.title: Mean and Variance: The Intuition
sections.content: Explain the expected value (mean = np) and variance (npq) as the 'center of mass' and 'spread' of the histogram, visually showing how changing 'p' shifts the distribution.
sections.example: If the robot dog has a 60% success rate, on average, how many successful jumps should we expect in 100 trials?

sections.title: Application and Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize how binomial distributions model real-world scenarios involving binary outcomes. Briefly touch upon how it relates to normal distribution approximations as n increases.
sections.example: Predicting success rates in quality control for a smartphone assembly line using binomial modeling.
